section_1.title: Introduction: The Dancing Line
section_1.content: Introduce the scenario of a set of finite points in a plane. Define the 'Windmill' process: A line passes through one point (the pivot) and rotates clockwise. When the line hits another point in the set, that new point becomes the pivot, and the rotation continues.
section_1.example: Imagine a dark field with several glowing fireflies (points). A single laser beam (the line) starts on one firefly and begins to spin like a clock hand. When it touches another firefly, the laser 'snaps' its center to that new firefly and keeps spinning.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: General Position & Rotation
section_2.content: Establish the necessary mathematical constraints: No three points are collinear (no 'triple hits') to ensure the pivot swap is unique. Introduce the concept that the line doesn't just rotate—it 'sweeps' the plane, and its orientation is defined by the angle (0 to 180 degrees).
section_2.example: Visualizing a 'Forbidden Configuration': Show three points in a straight line and explain why this would cause the 'Windmill' to break (it would hit two points at once). Show a protractor overlaying the pivot to track rotation.

section_3.title: Visualizing the Pivot Swap
section_3.content: Break down the mechanics of the 'hit and swap.' When the line rotates and hits point 'B' while pivoting on point 'A', the line effectively transitions its rotational axis. Emphasize that the line's direction is continuous even if the pivot changes.
section_3.example: Windy the Robot holds a long, straight pole. He stands on point A and spins. As soon as the pole touches point B, Windy teleports to point B and continues spinning the pole from the exact same angle.

section_4.title: The Core Invariant: Counting Sides
section_4.content: Introduce the 'Aha!' moment—the invariant. If we choose an initial line that divides the remaining points into two sets (S1 on the left, S2 on the right), what happens to the number of points on each side when a pivot swap occurs?
section_4.example: Color the points on the left side of the starting line Red and the points on the right side Blue. As the line hits a new point and swaps pivots, show that the number of Red points and Blue points remains constant because the line 'passes through' the point, moving it from one side of the pivot to the other side of the pivot, but keeping it on the same 'half-plane'.

section_5.title: The 180-Degree Flip
section_5.content: Explain what happens when the line has rotated 180 degrees. The line is the same set of points in space, but its 'direction' is reversed. This means the points that were on the 'left' are now on the 'right.'
section_5.example: Use a 'Two-Tone' line (Gold on one side, Silver on the other). After a 180-degree rotation, the Gold side now faces where the Silver side used to face. If there were 'k' points on the left initially, there must be 'k' points on the right now.

section_6.title: Conclusion: Infinite Connectivity
section_6.content: Conclude that because the number of points on each side stays constant (balanced) relative to the line's orientation, and the line must eventually return to its original position, every point will eventually serve as a pivot.
section_6.example: Show a time-lapse of the 'Windmill' completing a full 360-degree cycle. Highlight each firefly as it is touched, showing a 'glow' that stays lit, proving that every single firefly eventually becomes the center of the dance.

outline.example: Visualizing a 'Forbidden Configuration': Show three points in a straight line and explain why this would cause the 'Windmill' to break (it would hit two points at once). Show a protractor overlaying the pivot to track rotation.

outline.title: Conclusion: Infinite Connectivity
outline.content: Conclude that because the number of points on each side stays constant (balanced) relative to the line's orientation, and the line must eventually return to its original position, every point will eventually serve as a pivot.
outline.example: Show a time-lapse of the 'Windmill' completing a full 360-degree cycle. Highlight each firefly as it is touched, showing a 'glow' that stays lit, proving that every single firefly eventually becomes the center of the dance.

outline.title: Visualizing the Pivot Swap
outline.content: Break down the mechanics of the 'hit and swap.' When the line rotates and hits point 'B' while pivoting on point 'A', the line effectively transitions its rotational axis. Emphasize that the line's direction is continuous even if the pivot changes.
outline.example: Windy the Robot holds a long, straight pole. He stands on point A and spins. As soon as the pole touches point B, Windy teleports to point B and continues spinning the pole from the exact same angle.

outline.title: Introduction: The Dancing Line
outline.content: Introduce the scenario of a set of finite points in a plane. Define the 'Windmill' process: A line passes through one point (the pivot) and rotates clockwise. When the line hits another point in the set, that new point becomes the pivot, and the rotation continues.
outline.example: Imagine a dark field with several glowing fireflies (points). A single laser beam (the line) starts on one firefly and begins to spin like a clock hand. When it touches another firefly, the laser 'snaps' its center to that new firefly and keeps spinning.

outline.title: The 180-Degree Flip

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title = "Conclusion: Infinite Connectivity"
        lines = [
            "- The invariant forces the line to visit every point.",
            "- Each point eventually serves as the windmill's pivot.",
            "- Geometry and combinatorics unite to reveal this elegant pattern."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Define points (fireflies)
        dot_positions = ["C2", "B4", "A5", "D6", "F4", "E2"]
        dots = VGroup()
        for pos in dot_positions:
            dot = Dot(color=BLUE, radius=0.08)
            self.place_at_grid(dot, pos)
            dots.add(dot)
        
        self.add(dots)

        # Windmill line
        self.pivot_idx = 0
        line = Line(LEFT * 3.5, RIGHT * 3.5, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Using a closure-like mechanism with an attribute for the pivot index
        line.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_angle(angle_tracker.get_value()).move_to(dots[self.pivot_idx].get_center()))
        self.add(line)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Speed up rotation through multiple points to show the 'Dance'.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Rotate through dots
        rotation_steps = [
            (1, PI/4), (2, PI/2), (3, 3*PI/4), (4, PI), (5, 5*PI/4), (0, 3*PI/2)
        ]
        
        for idx, angle in rotation_steps:
            self.pivot_idx = idx
            self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(angle), run_time=0.4, rate_func=linear)
        
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Each point eventually serves as the windmill's pivot.
        # Draw the connection path (#FFFF00) formed by the pivots.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Define the connection path
        path_points = [dots[i].get_center() for i in [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 0]]
        connection_path = VMobject(color="#FFFF00", stroke_width=4)
        connection_path.set_points_as_corners(path_points)
        
        # Show the connection path being drawn
        self.play(Create(connection_path), run_time=2.5)
        
        # Add glow to all points to show they've been visited

            "Upon contact, the rotation axis shifts to that point.",
            "The line's direction remains continuous during this transition."
        ])

        point_b = Dot(color="#FF0000")

        line_length = 6

            pivot = pivot_mobject.get_location()
            angle = angle_tracker.get_value()
            direction = np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0])
            start = pivot - (line_length / 2) * direction
            end = pivot + (line_length / 2) * direction
            return [start, end]

        # The rotating line with updater for continuous transformation
        line = Line(*get_line_endpoints(), color=line_color, stroke_width=4)
        line.add_updater(lambda m: m.put_start_and_end_on(*get_line_endpoints()))

        self.add(point_a, point_b, label_a, label_b, line, tip1, tip2, trail1, trail2)
        
        # Calculate hitting angle where the line through A meets B
        pos_a = point_a.get_center()
        pos_b = point_b.get_center()
        diff = pos_b - pos_a
        hit_angle = np.arctan2(diff[1], diff[0])
        
        # Rotate clockwise from vertical (PI/2) to the hit_angle
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(hit_angle), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Upon contact, the rotation axis shifts to that point."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # White flash effect at both pivot points
        flash_a = Dot(pos_a, color=WHITE, radius=0.1)
        flash_b = Dot(pos_b, color=WHITE, radius=0.1)
        self.play(
            FadeIn(flash_a), FadeIn(flash_b),
            flash_a.animate.scale(5).set_opacity(0),
            flash_b.animate.scale(5).set_opacity(0),
            run_time=0.6
        )
        self.remove(flash_a, flash_b)
        
        # Shift pivot to point B
        pivot_mobject.move_to(pos_b)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "The line's direction remains continuous during this transition."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Continue clockwise rotation from the same angular direction
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(hit_angle - PI/2), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Reset color of the final lecture line
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)

In this section, we explore the 180-degree symmetry of the windmill line. When the line rotates exactly 180 degrees, it geometrically returns to its original position in space. However, its directed "left" and "right" half-planes have swapped places. This symmetry implies that for the line to return to an identical state with the same number of points on each side, the initial and final counts must be equal, reinforcing the invariant.

section_1.title: Introduction: The Dancing Line
section_1.content: Introduce the scenario of a set of finite points in a plane. Define the 'Windmill' process: A line passes through one point (the pivot) and rotates clockwise. When the line hits another point in the set, that new point becomes the pivot, and the rotation continues.
section_1.example: Imagine a dark field with several glowing fireflies (points). A single laser beam (the line) starts on one firefly and begins to spin like a clock hand. When it touches another firefly, the laser 'snaps' its center to that new firefly and keeps spinning.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: General Position & Rotation
section_2.content: Establish the necessary mathematical constraints: No three points are collinear (no 'triple hits') to ensure the pivot swap is unique. Introduce the concept that the line doesn't just rotate—it 'sweeps' the plane, and its orientation is defined by the angle (0 to 180 degrees).
section_2.example: Visualizing a 'Forbidden Configuration': Show three points in a straight line and explain why this would cause the 'Windmill' to break (it would hit two points at once). Show a protractor overlaying the pivot to track rotation.

section_3.title: Visualizing the Pivot Swap
section_3.content: Break down the mechanics of the 'hit and swap.' When the line rotates and hits point 'B' while pivoting on point 'A', the line effectively transitions its rotational axis. Emphasize that the line's direction is continuous even if the pivot changes.
section_3.example: Windy the Robot holds a long, straight pole. He stands on point A and spins. As soon as the pole touches point B, Windy teleports to point B and continues spinning the pole from the exact same angle.

section_4.title: The Core Invariant: Counting Sides
section_4.content: Introduce the 'Aha!' moment—the invariant. If we choose an initial line that divides the remaining points into two sets (S1 on the left, S2 on the right), what happens to the number of points on each side when a pivot swap occurs?
section_4.example: Color the points on the left side of the starting line Red and the points on the right side Blue. As the line hits a new point and swaps pivots, show that the number of Red points and Blue points remains constant because the line 'passes through' the point, moving it from one side of the pivot to the other side of the pivot, but keeping it on the same 'half-plane'.

section_5.title: The 180-Degree Flip
section_5.content: Explain what happens when the line has rotated 180 degrees. The line is the same set of points in space, but its 'direction' is reversed. This means the points that were on the 'left' are now on the 'right.'
section_5.example: Use a 'Two-Tone' line (Gold on one side, Silver on the other). After a 180-degree rotation, the Gold side now faces where the Silver side used to face. If there were 'k' points on the left initially, there must be 'k' points on the right now.

section_6.title: Conclusion: Infinite Connectivity
section_6.content: Conclude that because the number of points on each side stays constant (balanced) relative to the line's orientation, and the line must eventually return to its original position, every point will eventually serve as a pivot.
section_6.example: Show a time-lapse of the 'Windmill' completing a full 360-degree cycle. Highlight each firefly as it is touched, showing a 'glow' that stays lit, proving that every single firefly eventually becomes the center of the dance.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Start with a set of finite points in space.",
            "- A line passes through one point, called the pivot.",
            "- The line rotates clockwise around this pivot point.",
            "- It continues until it hits another point in the set.",
            "- The hit point becomes the new center of rotation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Dancing Line", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_POINTS = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_LINE = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_HIT = "#00FF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # - Start with a set of finite points in space.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_POINTS)
        points_pos = ["C3", "D4", "B2", "B5", "A4", "E2", "E5", "F3", "D1", "A6"]
        points = VGroup()
        for pos in points_pos:
            dot = Dot(color=COLOR_POINTS, radius=0.08)
            self.place_at_grid(dot, pos)
            points.add(dot)
            
        self.play(FadeIn(points))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # - A line passes through one point, called the pivot.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_LINE)
        pivot_point = points[0] # C3
        
        # Create a line long enough to span the local grid area
        line = Line(start=LEFT*3, end=RIGHT*3, color=COLOR_LINE)
        line.move_to(pivot_point.get_center())
        # Initial angle: 120 degrees
        line.rotate(120 * DEGREES) 
        
        self.play(Create(line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # - The line rotates clockwise around this pivot point.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_LINE)
        
        # Target angle calculation for D4 relative to C3
        v = points[1].get_center() - points[0].get_center()
        target_angle_rad = np.arctan2(v[1], v[0])
        current_angle_rad = 120 * DEGREES
        
        # Calculate clockwise rotation angle (negative)
        rot_angle = target_angle_rad - current_angle_rad
        while rot_angle > 0:
            rot_angle -= 2 * PI
            
        self.play(
            Rotate(line, angle=rot_angle, about_point=pivot_point.get_center()),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # - It continues until it hits another point in the set.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_HIT)
        hit_point = points[1]
        
        self.play(
            hit_point.animate.set_color(COLOR_HIT).scale(1.5),
            pivot_point.animate.set_color(COLOR_HIT).scale(1.5)
        )
        self.play(
            Flash(hit_point, color=COLOR_HIT),
            Flash(pivot_point, color=COLOR_HIT),
            hit_point.animate.scale(1/1.5),
            pivot_point.animate.scale(1/1.5)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # - The hit point becomes the new center of rotation.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_LINE) 
        
        # Scale up slightly to emphasize dancing motion
        everything = VGroup(points, line)
        self.play(everything.animate.scale(1.1))
        self.wait(2)

        # Grid positions for points (using a subset of the 6x6 grid)
        # Pivot initially at C3
        pivot_pos = self.grid["C3"]
        # 4 points on the left (x < pivot_x)
        left_pos_keys = ["A2", "B2", "D2", "E2"]
        # 4 points on the right (x > pivot_x)
        right_pos_keys = ["A4", "B4", "D4", "E4"]
        
        # Create point mobjects
        pivot_dot = Dot(pivot_pos, color=WHITE, radius=0.1)
        left_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(self.grid[p], color=WHITE, radius=0.08) for p in left_pos_keys])
        right_dots = VGroup(*[Dot(self.grid[p], color=WHITE, radius=0.08) for p in right_pos_keys])
        
        # Create count labels "4" for each side
        left_label = Text("4", font_size=36, color=COLOR_LEFT_LABEL)
        self.place_at_grid(left_label, "C1")
        right_label = Text("4", font_size=36, color=COLOR_RIGHT_LABEL)
        self.place_at_grid(right_label, "C5")

        # Rotating line setup using ValueTracker for angle and a persistent reference for the pivot
        line_angle = ValueTracker(PI/2) # Start with a vertical orientation
        self.current_pivot_pos = pivot_pos
        
        # Create the line mobject
        rotating_line = Line(ORIGIN, UP, color=COLOR_LINE, stroke_width=2)
        
        # Define a robust updater for the line
        def line_updater(l):
            angle = line_angle.get_value()
            p = self.current_pivot_pos
            direction = np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0])
            # Extend the line symmetrically from the pivot
            l.put_start_and_end_on(p - direction * 3.5, p + direction * 3.5)
            
        rotating_line.add_updater(line_updater)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Consider the points on each side of the line.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.add(pivot_dot, left_dots, right_dots)
        self.play(Create(rotating_line))
        self.wait(1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Color points on the left red and right blue.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            left_dots.animate.set_color(COLOR_RED),
            right_dots.animate.set_color(COLOR_BLUE),
            Write(left_label),
            Write(right_label)
        )
        self.wait(1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # As the pivot swaps, a point moves through the pivot.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Target point for swap: B4 (at index 1 in right_dots)
        # B4 (3.5, 1.2) from C3 (2.5, 0.2) is at angle PI/4 (45 degrees)
        target_angle_val = PI / 4.0
        
        # Rotate the line clockwise until it hits the target point
        self.play(line_angle.animate.set_value(target_angle_val), run_time=2.0, rate_func=linear)
        
        # Perform the pivot swap:
        # 1. B4 (right side) becomes the new white pivot.
        # 2. C3 (old pivot) moves to the right side and becomes blue.
        # This keeps the total counts (4 Red, 4 Blue) invariant.
        self.play(
            right_dots[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            pivot_dot.animate.set_color(COLOR_BLUE).set_radius(0.08),
            run_time=0.1
        )
        # Update the pivot position used by the line updater
        self.current_pivot_pos = self.grid["B4"]
        
        # Continue the rotation slightly to show the line passing through the new pivot
        self.play(line_angle.animate.set_value(target_angle_val - 0.2), run_time=1.0, rate_func=linear)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Crucially, the number of points on each side stays constant.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(
            Flash(left_label, color=COLOR_LEFT_LABEL, flash_radius=0.4),
            Flash(right_label, color=COLOR_RIGHT_LABEL, flash_radius=0.4),
            left_label.animate.scale(1.2),
            right_label.animate.scale(1.2)
        )
        self.play(
            left_label.animate.scale(1.0/1.2),
            right_label.animate.scale(1.0/1.2)
        )
        self.wait(1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This invariant is the key to solving the problem.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Final rotation to emphasize movement
        self.play(line_angle.animate.set_value(target_angle_val - 0.7), run_time=2.0)
        self.wait(2.0)
